answer: One defense is to make each identity expensive to fake. An agent earns trust only after it stakes a deposit and completes real, verifiable work over time, so spinning up a thousand clones costs a thousand deposits and a thousand work histories. Think of it like a mesa: the flat top looks easy to reach, but the climb is the proof. A summit meeting of agents could then check one clear signal, the stake and work record, and ignore any newcomer that shows up with neither.
